title: Markus Lehmusruusu’s Finnish Oscar Entry ‘The Squirrel’ Earns Aki Kaurismäki’s Stamp of Approval: ‘He Said It’s Like ‘2001: A Space Odyssey,’ but Better Because It’s Full of Humanism’
full_text: Sep 16, 2026 2:39am PT Markus Lehmusruusu’s Finnish Oscar Entry ‘The Squirrel’ Earns Aki Kaurismäki’s Stamp of Approval: ‘He Said It’s Like ‘2001: A Space Odyssey,’ but Better Because It’s Full of Humanism’ By Marta Balaga Plus Icon Marta Balaga Latest Markus Lehmusruusu’s Finnish Oscar Entry ‘The Squirrel’ Earns Aki Kaurismäki’s Stamp of Approval: ‘He Said It’s Like ‘2001: A Space Odyssey,’ but Better Because It’s Full of Humanism’ 4 hours ago Ali Asgari Doesn’t Believe in a Bright Future After Iran’s January Massacre – Just ‘A Bit of Light’ 3 days ago TIFF 2026: 20 International Titles to Track, From Feng-I Fiona Roan’s Shuhua Starrer to a Taxidermy Musical and a John Madden Parkinson’s Rom-Com 3 days ago See All Orava Max Smeds (Courtesy of Bufo) Markus Lehmusruusu ’s futuristic drama “ The Squirrel ” has just been selected as the Finnish Oscar submission, and it already has a notable fan. “ Aki Kaurismäki called it a masterpiece. He said it was like ‘2001: A Space Odyssey,’ but better because it’s full of humanism. I really loved that,” the director tells Variety . “I hope that it can work on two levels. It’s full of humanism, but it also shows that as humans, we shouldn’t always put ourselves first.” Related Stories Seth Green Says He Was Never Invited Back for the Canceled 'Buffy the Vampire Slayer' Reboot His protagonist, Pasi, needs to understand that as well. In the sterile future, nature and animals no longer exist. At least, that’s how it seems until Pasi, who designs artificial pets, suddenly encounters an actual squirrel – maybe the last one in the world. He brings it home, but it’s not happy there. It belongs in the wild. Popular on Variety “The Squirrel” stars Miro Lopperi (“Codename: Annika”), Mimosa Willamo (“Sisu”) and Hannu-Pekka Björkman (upcoming “Red Snow” ). Recently shown at Fantastic Fest, the film is sold by REinvent International Sales and produced by Bufo, Pallas Film, Volya Films and Zentropa Sweden. Being selected as an Oscar submission has been “rewarding,” says Lehmusruusu. “It’s a big risk to make a film like that, which doesn’t fit within one genre.” In recent years, Finland has selected several films that don’t fit the typical Oscar mold, from “Euthanizer” to “Family Time” and boozy comedy “100 Liters of Gold.” It has only earned one nomination in the category, for Aki Kaurismäki’s “The Man Without a Past.” “It’s about telling stories that come from the heart without overthinking where they ‘fit’,” notes Lehmusruusu. “Now, I’m working on projects that feel almost naturalistic, but I’ve always been interested in films that depict someone’s inner world. Cinema can convey that so easily. It’s like a magic trick.” For his characters, the situation is clear: animalistic urges are bad. But as the story progresses, they want to give in to them. “Thanks to technology, we sometimes feel omnipotent. But wouldn’t something be missing if replaced nature with something that doesn’t have its downsides?,” wonders Lehmusruusu. “This also led to sexuality being a big part of the film because we keep hearing about people not having sex anymore. Young people just aren’t interested, partly because they’re repulsed by bodily fluids. Sexuality is perhaps the most primal force we have left, and we are becoming detached from it.” Luckily, it only takes one squirrel to open his characters’ eyes and encourage them to venture outside of their comfort zones. Even though they’re so used to controlling their bodies and their surroundings. The film’s naughty, not-quite-PG side is perfectly exemplified by its titular hero. “A squirrel is cute, but it’s also a rodent. They destroy things in people’s houses and attack small birds. I wanted to show how we project onto animals. We think we know their emotions. At one point, we wondered if our squirrel should have expressions, but then I went: ‘I don’t want it to do anything it doesn’t actually do.’ It’s one of those animals we take for granted. And when you take something for granted, it’s so painful when it’s gone.” Instead of choosing obvious villains, Lehmusruusu talks about “the consequences of indifference” in the film. “I wanted to show people who have good intentions, but they have gone too far. We like to think we’re protecting our families or societies, but what are we willing to sacrifice? It could be nature or another form of life,” he says. “My idea was to go against this dystopian science fiction where evil is always lurking. In a way, it feels even darker to say that people aren’t bad; they are just making bad choices. As a species, we’re responsible for a lot of shit.” However, sometimes we are able to clean it up. “If you look at the bigger picture, the horror of it all slowly sneaks up on you. But I wanted this film to work also if you’re not willing to do that. title: ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Season 35 Premiere Recap: The Men Take The Lead In First Of Two-Night Kick Off & Someone Goes Home Already
full_text: Skip to main content By Katie Campione Katie Campione Senior TV & Labor Reporter @katie_campione More Stories By Katherine ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Season 35 Premiere Recap: The Men Take The Lead In First Of Two-Night Kick Off & Someone Goes Home Already Emmys Producers Dish On Taylor Swift ‘SVU’ Sketch (Including The Easter Eggs), Mariska Hargitay’s Hosting Chops, Dolly Parton Tribute & More Sally Field Reflects On Filming ‘Remarkably Bright Creatures’ In Canada: “Let’s Keep Our Neighbors Close” — Emmys Backstage View All September 15, 2026 6:59pm 'Dancing With The Stars' Season 35 ABC SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from night one of the Season 35 premiere of Dancing with the Stars . Back like they never left! The ballroom at CBS Television City was once again glittering with celebrities on Tuesday night to kick off Season 35 of Dancing with the Stars. There are 16 contestants vying for the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy at the top of the season, and ABC opted for a two-night premiere that split the dances between Tuesday and Wednesday nights. On the first night, only the male celebrities performed. The ladies will take the floor on Wednesday night. Related Stories News 'American Idol' Moving Production To Georgia As ABC Series Becomes Latest To Leave California News 'Dancing With The Stars' Pro Emma Slater Pulls Out Stops By Performing With Savannah Bananas Ahead Of Tuesday's Premiere Unfortunately, things did not go over without a hitch. The party was interrupted by some tech issues, with voting going down online in the middle of the show. They threw out the ABC.com votes mid-premiere and relied solely on text votes, which have their own wrinkle this year since there’s two contestants who share the same name. Voters will need to specify Conner L. or Connor W. in their text votes, and they won’t count if they don’t, according to hosts Afonso Ribeiro and Julianne Hough. What could go wrong there? Watch on Deadline While this week’s results might be questionable, the show must go on. Here’s how things shook out on night one. Savannah Bananas midfielder Jackson Olson with Emma Slater. The baseball player kicked things off with a cha cha to “Wannabe” by the Spice Girls — and it’s clear that Slater is reveling in being paired with a younger partner this season. In the package before the dance, she said it’s the first time she’s ever worked with a celeb in their 20s, and admits there were less “limitations” working with Olson.The energetic routine was a nice introduction to Olson, and the judges ate it up. “The ballroom is back!” judge Derek Hough said. “Jackson, my man, you are a natural born performer.” BUT! Hough also warned that the judges are going to be pretty tough with their scores this season, and Olson has plenty of room for improvement in the technique department. SCORE: 15 out of 30 Reality star Tyler Cameron with Sharna Burgess. The Bachelor alum was the first of many reality stars to take the dance floor over the next two days, dancing a tango. The former college football player says he did take some dance classes in college, but he’s got some brushing up to do. After a multi-year hiatus from the show, Burgess pleased the judges with her first routine with Cameron. “Tyler, what’s going on here? I have to say, I’m very pleasantly surprised. I mean, look at him. He looks like a tank…you can move, man,” Bruno Tonioli complimented. SCORE: 17 out of 30 Reality star Conner Leavitt with Adele Zaikman. These two stepped onto the ballroom floor with something to prove Tuesday night, what with newcomer Zaikman as the winner of DWTS: The Next Pro and Leavitt married to Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star Whitney Leavitt, who took the ballroom by storm last season and leveraged the exposure to launch a Broadway run on Chicago . They danced a salsa to “Whoomp! (There It Is)” by Tag Team, putting Zaikman in her element as a Latin expert and taking Leavitt straight out of his. Carrie Ann Inaba called the routine “a little chaotic,” but overall, the judges loved the enthusiasm. SCORE: 12 out of 30 Late-night sidekick Guillermo Rodriguez with Witney Carson. Season 34 champ Carson is back on the ballroom floor with a much different contestant this year. She’s guiding Jimmy Kimmel’s right-hand man Rodriguez through the competition, and they started off with a cha cha. Carson, who is impressively competing pregnant this year, tried to disguise her partner’s lack of technique by leaning into Rodriguez’s charm, reminding why he’s spent decades at Kimmel’s side on late night. It only kind of worked. “Listen, was the technique there? No. Was the effort there? Absolutely,” Hough said. “We can’t be having heel leads in the cha cha.” Regardless, the audience clearly responded to Rodriguez’s “spicy” performance, chanting his name when he finished. There were even boos when the judges issued their (probably rightful) rating. SCORE: 10 out of 30 Paralympian Ezra Frech with Daniella Karagach. Julianne Hough kind of botched his introduction, but Frech still made a great impression on his first night as his rehearsal package gave audiences a glimpse of what he’s working through this season as an above-the-knee amputee in the competition. He and Karagach had to make some accommodations to take on the tango, but boy, did they deliver. The judges loved the fiery routine to Kelly Clarkson’s “Since U Been Gone,” and so did the crowd. “What really impressed me, you really looked like a leading man,” Tonioli said. SCORE: 20 out 30 Comedian and podcaster Connor Wood with Rylee Arnold. The second Connor of the night showcased his personality with a cha cha to “I Like It, I Love It” by Tim McGraw. Of the group, Wood has some of the least dance experience, so it appears Arnold may have her work cut out for her this season. But what he lacks in technique, he makes up for in his sincerity. On the bright side, Inaba says he didn’t give her “the ick” when he made a wrong move. A for effort! No comment on the person riding a bedazzled mechanical bull in the background for the entire number. SCORE: 16 out of 30 Musician Taylor Hanson with Britt Stewart. The middle Hanson brother is back on stage after spending years “avoiding dancing.” He says he’s uncomfortable performing without an instrument in tow, but Stewart tells him to think of her as his new “safety blanket.” Having gone from avoiding all dancing to taking on the quickstep night one, Derek Hough assures him he should feel proud, despite the flaws. Tonioli agreed. Now, he needs to work on his frame. “Don’t tighten up,” Tonioli said. SCORE: 16 out of 30 Actor Harry Shum Jr. with Jenna Johnson. The Glee and Grey’s Anatomy actor closed out the night one with yet another cha cha. Johnson took advantage of Shum’s freestyle and hip-hop experience, though, and his prior performance chops on Glee to deliver a performance full of personality and charm. And, well, they absolutely saved the best for last. Those two lit up the ballroom floor with an “emergency disco” that had Tonioli in a fit. “The chemistry between you two is off the charts. Sharp as a scalpel,” he said. SCORE: 21 out of 30 (the highest score of the night!) So, who goes home? Sadly, after just one dance, Conner Leavitt and Adele Zaikman are sent packing. Well, they’ll be back in the ballroom at least once more for tomorrow’s ‘live afterparty’ with Season 34 winner Robert Irwin and whomever among the women is voted off on night two. title: ‘Possible Love’ DoP Kim Ji-yong, ‘The Blue Road’ Director Han Jun-hee & WETA FX’s Kimball Thurston Among Speakers For Netflix ‘Creative Asia’ At BIFF
full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz ‘Possible Love’ DoP Kim Ji-yong, ‘The Blue Road’ Director Han Jun-hee & WETA FX’s Kimball Thurston Among Speakers For Netflix ‘Creative Asia’ At BIFF Goodfellas Boards World Sales On Kamila Andini’s ‘Four Seasons In Java’ Ahead Of Toronto Premiere Finecut Scores Sales On Trio Of Titles Starring Members Of K-Pop Groups NCT, Fifty Fifty & The Boyz View All September 15, 2026 7:14pm Busan International Film Festival Busan International Film Festival Netflix has announced that speakers including Possible Love DoP Kim Ji-yong, The Blue Road director Han Jun-hee and WETA FX’s CTO Kimball Thurston will join the streamer’s Creative Asia programme at this year’s Busan International Film Festival (BIFF). Ji-yong will deliver a masterclass on how he and Possible Love director Lee Chang-dong shaped the visual world of the film, which just scored the Grand Jury Prize in Venice and is Korea’s official section for the Oscars. Han Jun-hee, whose credits also include D.P. and Weak Hero Class , is hosting a masterclass entitled “Making Unexpected Stories Resonate” about turning unexpected, even uncomfortable, subjects into stories that capture the world’s attention. Related Stories News Alix Earle's Reality Series 'Earle Meets World' Finds More Viewers In Week Two News 'The Murder Of JonBenét Ramsey' Gets December Release Date On Netflix & First-Look Photo Of Melissa McCarthy & Clive Owen As Girl's Parents Creative Asia will also feature a masterclass on “Location and Storytelling”, bringing together perspectives from Lauren Cooper of Location Managers Guild International, Perfect Days producer Reiko Kunieda and Sung Q Lee, Senior Director, APAC Production at Netflix. Watch on Deadline WETA FX’s chief technology officer Kimball Thurston is one of the speakers on an industry panel about using AI in filmmaking – “AI in Filmmaking: New Tools, New Possibilities” – along with Sung Q Lee and Korean director Kang Yun-sung ( Run To The West , The Outlaws ). Another industry panel entitled “New Voices in Filmmaking: What’s Ahead” will examine small- to medium-budget filmmaking and features speakers including Namkoong Sun ( Love Untangled ) and Wi Eun-kyoung and Son Gwang-min, co-directors of My Aunt . The programme also includes two workshops: “The Art and Archetypes of Cinematic Storytelling”, led by Netflix’s Director, Content Acquisition, Christopher Mack, is aimed at writers and breaks down what makes a pilot compelling and the structural choices that keep audiences watching. Led by Netflix’s Director, Creative Strategy, “Understanding the Buyer’s Perspective” looks at what motivates greenlight decisions, how a show gets chosen for financing, and what kind of script or story stays in the imagination after a pitch ends. Designed to support the region’s next generation of creators, the programme has been devised by Netflix in partnership with BIFF, the Asian Film Commissions Network (AFCNet) and the Motion Picture Association (MPA). It will take place on October 10 at Dongseo University Centum Campus. BIFF is running October 6-15 at the Busan Cinema Center and locations across Busan, with the Asian Contents & Film Market taking place at BEXCO October 10-13. A longtime Key Second Assistant Director on the Jason Segel and Harrison Ford starring series says she was abruptly fired after a long day of shooting on July 10 by Executive Producer Kip Kroeger because of so-called “different needs of production.” In her seven claim compliant filed today in L.A. Superior Court against WBTV, Shrinking EP/director Randall Winston and others, Mindy Tessa McKoin doesn’t buy it. Related Stories News Emmy TV Ratings Down 10% From Last Year News Amazon In Talks To Take Over Emmys TV Deal As the document from attorney Avi Gholian exclaims of the industry vet’s multi-season Shrinking stint: “no performance deficiency, misconduct. or business rationale was identified then or anytime thereafter.” Watch on Deadline Filing earlier today with the California Civil Rights Department before going to the LASC docket, McKoin alleges the real reason she was canned was because of reporting an intentional “sexual abuse” by Winston at the June 22, 2024 Shrinking Season 2 wrap party, She says it was because of that and because of her raising a stink about of “inaccurate time records and pay statements.” Production and WBTV problems that Loot and Young Sheldon alum McKoin and her lawyers assert resulted in zero “corrective action” on the former and a lot of her Shrinking bosses not making a “big deal” about the former. McKoin says the CAA-repped Winston subjected her “to unwelcome, severe harassment because of her sex, including by grabbing and groping her breast without her consent at a work-related function in the presence of a coworker” at the 2024 party. “Such conduct was sufficiently severe to alter the conditions of Plaintiff employment and to create a hostile, intimidating, and offensive working environment.” An environment made all the worse by WBTV doing nothing about it, according to the plaintiff. While the sexual harassment and sexual battery claims sit on the top of McKoin’s allegations, it is the pay and timecard tampering of sorts that takes up the bulk of Tuesday’s unspecified damages seeking filing. In terms of retaliation, McKoin insists she made “bona fide complaints, both orally and in writing, that she was owed unpaid wages and that her time records had been unlawfully altered, and otherwise engaged in conduct protected by the Labor Code, including on or about May 26, May 28, June I0, June 11, June 19, and July I, 2026.” Her filing adds: “Warner Bros. discharged Plaintiff on July 10, 2026 – within 90 days of each of these instances of protected activities. “ “ As a direct and proximate result of Warner Bros.’ violation of Labor Code …Plaintiff has suffered and continues to suffer lost wages and work benefits and other actual consequential, and incidental financial losses. as well as emotional distress. humiliation, mental anguish, and anxiety in an amount to be proven at trial.” WBTV had no comment this evening when contacted by Deadline about the complaint and the allegations McKoin makes. Representatives for the multi-Emmy nominated Winston did no response when Deadline reached out about the claims against their client. title: Seriesly Berlin Crowns ‘Hands Up’, Music Drama Featuring Israeli & Palestinian Characters
full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Seriesly Berlin Crowns ‘Hands Up’, Music Drama Featuring Israeli & Palestinian Characters True Crime Remains The Red Hot TV Doc Genre, Ampere Data Shows PBS Buys Dutch Dementia Doc ‘Human Forever’, Which Follows “The Greta Thunberg Of Healthcare” View All September 15, 2026 11:21pm Creatives behind 'Hands Up' with the Writers Award jury after win Seriesly Berlin Seriesly Berlin kept up its reputation for backing complex TV series with its latest batch of award winners. Hands Up , a music drama series pitch from the U.S. focused on an Israeli musician and a Palestinian singer brought together in Berlin’s hip-hop scene was the winner of the Writers’ Pitch Award last night at a ceremony near the Fotografiska in Germany’s capital. The pitch was a popular winner, with the jury unanimous on the victor and several people we spoke to agreeing on the choice. The audience cheered wildly as the announcement was made. Related Stories News True Crime Remains The Red Hot TV Doc Genre, Ampere Data Shows News Seriesly Berlin Unveils Full Line-Up With Sessions On 'Krank Berlin', Creative Tensions & Co-Productions “ Hands Up has all the ingredients to be a great series: a clear central conflict, extraordinary characters, and even great music,” said the Seriesly Berlin jury in a statement. “It is a perfect example of a hyper local premise that can serve as a metaphor, touching audiences around the world. This story shows us that creative collaboration can bridge impossible borders, providing a path to mutual understanding in troubled times.” Watch on Deadline Coming from Neta Weiner, Samira Saraya and Michal Cooper Keren and borne out of the U.S., the story follows Israeli musician Geva and Palestinian singer Manal, who join together for a high-stakes collaboration set up by Petra, a former music industry figure who sees in their volatile chemistry a chance for a comeback of her own. As their music gains traction, their growing fame soon turns dangerous, and they are caught between political pressure, family expectations and ongoing public scrutiny, forcing them to risk relationships, their future and even their lives for the freedom to be heard. Palestinian artist, actress and filmmaker Saraya and Jewish rapper, musician and actor Weiner have worked across music, theater and screen as activists whose work explores identity, politics, and resistance. They were members of a Palestinian-Jewish hip-hop group and founders of a cultural education initiative. Israeli screenwriter and showrunner Keren has worked on shows for HBO Go, Canal+, Disney, Rai, Nickelodeon and Netflix. The show beat of pitches from Ireland, Germany, Serbia and the UK to win the Writers Pitch award, and takes home a €1,000 ($1,150) prize. Elsewhere, Latvian drama The Man Behind a Mask ( Cilvēks Maskā ) won the Co-Pro Pitch Award and landed a €25,000 post-production services prize. The show, from creator Anna Kalnina and producer Serge Serpuhovs, follows celebrated Soviet reconstructive surgeon Nikolay, who pioneers groundbreaking procedures, including the USSR’s first sex reassignment surgery, until the KGB blackmails him into espionage. Per the snyopsis, “His missions take him across Europe and beyond, where each medical breakthrough becomes a covert operation. Torn between his calling as a healer and his role as a spy, Nikolay is forced to betray patients, outwit intelligence agencies, and confront impossible moral choices. In the end, he survives, but returns home forever changed, having lost both his innocence and his faith in the regime.” The jury said it was “an engaging story about power and vulnerabilities, set in an original arena and based on true events that uses spy thriller elements to create a highly entertaining show for an international audience with the potential to run for multiple seasons.” The SteinbrennerMüller Award, which is handed out by Berlin-based PR firm SteinbrennerMüller Kommunkation to a German show with the best potential to connect with audiences, went to Hannah Doose’s I Am God ( Ich Bin Gott ). The show follows eight middle-aged people in midlife who come together at a spiritual festival on the German-Polish border. Amid cacao ceremonies, breathwork and psychedelic rituals, relationships begin to unravel, families drift apart and old wounds resurface, as the festival organizers ignore warnings of an approaching tornado. “The premise is a very clear promise of entertainment – world-building set in a nature reserve on the border between Germany and Poland,” said a rep from SteinbrennerMüller. “ I Am God explores social issues in a light-hearted yet relevant way through exaggeration. “This closed setting allows for the creation of characters who reflect all facets of society and with whom a wide audience can identify, combined with plenty of fun. Hovering over it all is the looming threat of an approaching tornado, which could wipe out all those ‘first world problems’ in an instant.” Mayana FIlms is the producer, with Doose writing alongside Nicolas Chevaillier and Sarah Schill. Chevaillier and Zorana Mušikić are the producers. The Seriesly Berlin conference ends today. title: Cate Blanchett To Attend Tokyo Film Festival With Displacement Film Fund Shorts
full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Oscars: Spain Selects ‘La Bola Negra’ For International Feature Film Race Cate Blanchett To Attend Tokyo Film Festival With Displacement Film Fund Shorts Screamfest To Open With ‘The Night Driver’ Starring Josh Lucas, David Arquette & Alyssa Milano View All September 16, 2026 12:31am Cate Blanchett speaks on stage during the Cannes Film Festival Teresa Suarez/Pool/Getty Images Cate Blanchett will attend this year’s Tokyo Film Festival with a series of short films supported by her Displacement Film Fund . TIFF will screen five short works produced with support from the Displacement Film Fund, of which Japanese brand Uniqlo is a founding partner. Following the film screenings, there will be a Q&A session with director Mohammad Rasoulof, director Shahrbanoo Sadat ( Super Afghan Gym ), and Blanchett. The screenings will take place the same week that Blanchett is to be honored in Tokyo with the festival’s Praemium Imperiale Award. “I am privileged to have the opportunity to share the inaugural short films supported through the Displacement Film Fund with audiences at Tokyo International Film Festival,” Blanchett said in a statement. title: Disney Seeking Next Big K-Pop Hit After Striking Ten-Project Deal With Kakao

Disney Korea has struck a deal with Kakao Entertainment to launch what they are calling a “K-culture fund” and is aiming to pursue around 10 projects over the medium to long term. The pair will “collaborate on projects that bring together K-pop IP and Disney’s stories and characters,” they saiid, “aiming to take the K-IP ecosystem to the next level and create new opportunities on the global stage.” Disney and Kakao stressed that the “K-culture fund” still needs to be ironed out, but they hope to do it. Neither company put a figure on the fund. title: Jodie Whittaker To Star As Hotshot Media Lawyer In ITV Drama ‘In Contempt’
full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Seriesly Berlin Crowns ‘Hands Up’, Music Drama Featuring Israeli & Palestinian Characters True Crime Remains The Red Hot TV Doc Genre, Ampere Data Shows PBS Buys Dutch Dementia Doc ‘Human Forever’, Which Follows “The Greta Thunberg Of Healthcare” View All September 16, 2026 1:30am Jodie Whittaker Pip in London for CLD Communications EXCLUSIVE: Jodie Whittaker ‘s next starring role will be a hotshot media lawyer in ITV drama In Contempt . Ahead of her role in Hulu pilot Chicks and a part in the London-set Only Murders in the Building Season 6, Whittaker will star in the “high-stakes” legal drama as barrister Olivia Savareid. The character’s top-drawer advocacy skills have built her a career defending people’s reputations and engaging in multi-million pound litigation to prevent their names from being destroyed on social media, but the series will see the tables turned on her. Related Stories News International Revenues Of $2.1B Boost British TV Makers, Census Finds, As Pact Warns BBC Must Avoid "Managed Decline" News Tom Jones Claims He Has Been Fired From 'The Voice UK' Because Of "Financial Difficulty" Sherlock and Dracula maker Hartswood Films is producing in association with its parent, ITV Studios (ITVS), with the show airing in the UK on ITV and STV and on streamers ITVX and STV Player. ITVS has international distribution rights. Watch on Deadline Steve Thompson ( Sherlock ) is the writer, with Sue Vertue and Steven Moffat the executive producers. Ed Bazalgette ( The Last Kingdom ) is the director and Lawrence Till ( Douglas is Cancelled ) the producer. ITV’s Director of Drama, Polly Hill, who commissioned the show is also overseeing production for the broadcaster. In Contempt establishes Olivia’s challenging working relationship with veteran news director Greg Dalman, who edits a London daily newspaper prone to pushing the boundaries of what can be published. With a reputation for taking no prisoners, Greg has the capability of acting recklessly if he believes it’s in the public interest, and and as his legal counsel, Olivia, must summon all her skills and expertise to keep him out of libel court. She is also the mother of 15-year-old daughter, but when an explosive situation erupts at work, she makes a crucial misjudgement and Olivia’s own reputation is suddenly on the line. “There’s always been a voracious appetite for what happens behind the scenes before news stories are published,” said ITV’s Hill. “Steve has created a gripping and thought-provoking series and I’m thrilled Jodie Whittaker has agreed to play ‘hotshot’ lawyer Olivia Savereid. I have no doubt In Contempt will captivate our audience, as it’s a really timely story for ITV to be telling.” Whittaker, known for leading Doctor Who and ITV drama Broadchurch , said of her role as Savareid. “This is an amazing character in a world I haven’t explored before. Steve Thompson’s writing is an absolute joy to work with and I’m so excited to be embarking on this adventure with such a brilliant creative team at Hartswood Films and ITV.” Vertue said she had been seeking to work with Thompson again since BBC series Sherlock , but that “it was never the right time or the right idea” until now. “Then one day he sat down and said, “In the modern world, if you want to kill someone, you don’t use a gun – you destroy their reputation,’ and so began In Contempt . “A whirlwind drama of cancellation, online poison and media law, where there’s less than 12 hours to stop a headline that could detonate someone’s life. This is the story of now, and this is the series for today. I’m delighted to be working with ITV again and to bring to screen Steve Thompson’s most explosive and personal drama yet.” Thompson called the show “a signature piece for me”, adding: “It unpacks the challenging relationship between the media and the law – between the freedom of the press and people’s right to privacy. In a world where all of us are surfing the net, hungry for the latest gossip, this drama takes us behind the curtain and shows us the lawyers who are in the vanguard of that fight.” In Contempt will begin filming in London in the fall with further casting coming closer to production commencing. title: Bill Nighy Playing Socially-Challenged Literary Titan In Richard Curtis’ Debut Audio Sitcom
full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max ‘Hunting Gary Glitter’: Netflix Unveils Trailer & Launch Date For Doc About Race To Expose Serial Sex Abuser Bill Nighy Playing Socially-Challenged Literary Titan In Richard Curtis’ Debut Audio Sitcom Disney Seeking Next Big K-Pop Hit After Striking Ten-Project Deal With Kakao View All September 16, 2026 2:00am Richard Curtis (left) and Bill Nighy Rich Hardcastle / Aliona Adrianova EXCLUSIVE: Richard Curtis is returning to the sitcom game, this time through audio. The Vicar of Dibley, Blackadder and Mr Bean writer-director is making Greatest Living Writer for BBC Radio 4 starring Bill Nighy , Nicola Walker, Nick Mohammed, Jim Broadbent, Meera Syal and Traitors star Madelyn Smedley. It is Curtis’ first sitcom in nearly 20 years and his first for audio. Launching on Boxing Day on Radio 4 and as a BBC Sounds box-set two weeks prior, the series centers on John Westlake (Nighy), a literary titan whose towering genius has earned him global reverence, lifelong indulgence, and absolutely no useful social skills. As those around him absorb the blast radius of his genius, the series plays with creativity, legacy, literary celebrity, family, and the uncomfortable truth that being good at writing does not necessarily make you good at being a pleasant person. The character draws comparisons with the iconic Billy Mack, who Nighy played with aplomb in Love Actually. Watch on Deadline His last TV sitcom was The Vicar of Dibley, which concluded on the BBC in 2007. He has recently turned to animation: writing and producing Netflix’s That Christmas in 2024 and now producing Not Alone for Universal. Curtis said: “I’m loving working in this tight 15” minute format for the BBC – writing for performers I know and love – and writing something that’s about the creative world I have such direct experience of, as it crashes into family dynamics.” Script editor Emma Freud added: “Of all his writing, this is the closest Richard has written to his life, his world, his home and his experiences. It’s been a joy to see the scripts flowing out of him – I’ve never seen him write so fast or enjoy the process as much. He isn’t the brute at the centre of this comedy – but that brute is, I think, how he would secretly like to behave if he could. Which he can’t.” Goldhawk Productions ‘ Greatest Living Writer is produced by Emma Hearn, John Scott Dryden and Alex Hollands and script edited by Freud. It comes on a BBC audio slate that includes pilots from Nish Kumar and Jake Bhardwaj, along with stand-up and quiz shows.
